newsitem.title: INDIA: Hindu party stalls India parliament over Pakistan.
newsitem.headline: Hindu party stalls India parliament over Pakistan.

text.p: India's Hindu opposition party on Thursday stalled proceedings in parliament over proposed talks with Pakistan, saying New Delhi must not give unilateral concessions to its Islamic neighbour.
"There should be no unilateral concessions. Why should there be no reciprocity?" said Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) deputy Pramod Mahajan, forcing a brief adjournment of the lower house of parliament.
"We want to know from the government why the proposed visa relaxation the foreign minister has announced cannot be linked with the release of Indian soldiers in Pakistani prisons," Mahajan said.

Indian officials quoted Foreign Minister Inder Gujral as saying he proposed to relax restrictions on visas for Pakistani businessmen and journalists to boost "people-to-people contact" between the two neighbours, who have fought three wars since 1947.
Top-level bilateral talks, stalled since January 1994, are scheduled to begin on March 28. Gujral told Reuters on Wednesday he proposed to open up trade with Pakistan.

The BJP, a hardline Hindu nationalist party, opposes any talks with Pakistan unless they include the issue of alleged terrorism that it says Islamabad promotes in the disputed territory of Kashmir. Pakistan says it provides only moral and diplomatic support to separatist rebels in the Himalayan region.
